text: The store managers' report is live. Now we build the foundation of the VP's side of the platform: a Power BI semantic model connected directly to the warehouse, with relationships and core measures written once so every future chart agrees.

Three model decisions matter most: Import mode, since this is a nightly-refreshed dataset, not a live query target; every dimension-to-fact relationship set single-direction, never bidirectional; and dim_date explicitly marked as the model's date table -- skip that last one, and time-intelligence functions quietly return wrong numbers.
Core measures live in one dedicated table, written with CALCULATE rather than raw column sums, so Total Net Sales means exactly one thing no matter which visual references it.

Time intelligence -- year-over-year, trailing seven days -- only works because dim_date was marked as a date table first. Before building a single visual, we check one measure against one store and one day by hand against last lesson's SSRS report -- they agree to the cent.
The calculation engine is trustworthy. Next: the actual dashboard the VP of Operations opens every morning.
